originality.rationale: The inspected 2020 primary text gives open-neighborhood Johnson/Hamming VC bounds and, in Corollary 4.4, identifies the rank-two complete-graph subdivision as an induced Hamming neighborhood; this graph identification is prior and is not claimed. The 2024 hedgehog text uses the same complete uniform-incidence graph but proves induced Turan extremal bounds, not closed-neighborhood support counts. No accessible earlier theorem was found implying the piecewise maximum-support count, the rank/corank closed-neighborhood VC formula, or the rank-two Littlestone separation. value.rationale: The graph is a canonical incidence structure for all k-subsets. Its closed-neighborhood class has a previously unreported, sharply rank/corank-dependent VC law; the count and classification of every maximum shattered support for all ranks are natural exact extremal invariants, not arbitrary small slices. The rank-two family supplies a precise VC/Littlestone separation and the open-versus-closed neighborhood comparison can increase VC dimension by two. These facts can inform graph-definable trace complexity, learning examples, and incidence-family enumeration without requiring a downstream theorem.
